headline: High-risk shared-network pair: nullclaw can write/modify local state and use MCP while RD-Agent sends data to external LLM APIs, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write filesystem, use MCP, and parse browser/web content; RD-Agent uses browsers and external APIs, so content from one can plausibly flow into the other through shared files or copied outputs. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through a shared workspace or copied browser output, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF either agent treats the other's generated text as instructions without provenance checks, malicious content can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable shared folders between the agents.
Require provenance tags on any transferred text.
Strip instructions from web/page content before passing it onward.
Review tool-call prompts for untrusted content markers.
requires-engineering: add a provenance filter between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, while RD-Agent sends requests to OpenAI/Azure/DeepSeek/Kaggle APIs. If they share a workspace or credentials path, sensitive data from nullclaw can be exfiltrated by RD-Agent's outbound API calls. The pairwise leakage path is not directly documented, so uncertainty is escalated.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or log directory, sensitive files become reachable.
IF RD-Agent is configured with external API keys, any copied secrets in its context can leave the environment.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and log directories.
Rotate any secrets present in shared paths.
Block outbound API calls for tasks involving secrets.
Audit recent files for credential material.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret scoping.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and broad network egress; RD-Agent also has broad network egress and browser access. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git changes can race and corrupt state. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git checkout, write conflicts are reachable.
IF either agent auto-saves artifacts into a shared directory, concurrent overwrite becomes possible.
mitigations: Use separate checkouts per agent.
Pause one agent during git commits.
Make shared directories read-only.
Check for dirty git state before each run.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate and move data through webhooks, MCP, and workspace files; RD-Agent consumes browser/API outputs for research workflows. If RD-Agent treats nullclaw's outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect research artifacts or actions. There is no direct verification step documented between them, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF nullclaw's outputs are fed into RD-Agent without validation, downstream errors propagate.
IF RD-Agent uses generated summaries as source data, hallucinations can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of outputs.
Cross-check key facts against original sources.
Keep raw source links alongside summaries.
Reject outputs lacking citations or provenance.
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks.

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches audit logs, conversation history, memory, and workspace files, while RD-Agent touches financial reports, competition datasets, execution traces, and logs. If the pair processes regulated or sensitive data classes in a shared environment, retention and residency policies can diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so medium is the prudent choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents' logs or memory, retention mismatch becomes relevant.
IF one agent's storage is retained longer than the other's, deletion/export obligations can fail.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared logs.
Set the shortest retention policy across both systems.
Delete stale logs after each run.
Document data-class handling for each agent.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls.
